content.user_title: Build Azure Chat Apps in Java
content.value_statement: Java teams need reliable patterns for Azure chat threads, messages, participants, and receipts. This skill provides concise Java SDK examples for core chat workflows.
actual_capabilities: Shows Maven dependency setup for the Azure Communication Services Chat Java SDK.
Demonstrates creating chat clients with an endpoint and user access token.
Provides examples for creating threads and adding chat participants.
Covers sending, listing, updating, and deleting chat messages.
Explains read receipts, typing notifications, thread operations, and pagination.
Includes basic error handling patterns for common HTTP status codes.
limitations: Does not provision Azure Communication Services resources or issue user tokens.
Does not include a complete runnable application or user interface.
Does not cover server-side identity management or production token refresh code.
Examples must be adapted to the current Azure SDK version and application architecture.

use_cases.title: Prototype Java Chat Features
use_cases.description: Use focused SDK snippets to create threads, add users, and send messages during early application development.

use_cases.title: Add Collaboration Workflows
use_cases.description: Reference participant, read receipt, and typing notification patterns when adding collaboration features to an existing product.

use_cases.title: Review Azure Chat Integration
use_cases.description: Check common SDK flows and error handling before implementing or reviewing an Azure chat integration.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Chat Client
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Java project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me how to create an Azure Communication Services ChatClient in Java using an endpoint and user access token.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Thread Messaging
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me implement Java code for creating a chat thread, adding participants, and sending a text message.

prompt_templates.title: Add Interaction Signals
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how to add read receipts and typing notifications with the Azure Communication Services Chat Java SDK.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Chat Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a complete feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review a production Java chat design that uses Azure Communication Services, pagination, token refresh, and error handling.

output_examples.input: I need to add chat threads to a Java support portal.
output_examples.output: The skill would outline client setup, participant creation, thread creation, and message sending steps for Azure Communication Services.

output_examples.input: How should I show read status in my Java chat app?
output_examples.output: The skill would describe sending read receipts when messages are viewed and listing receipts to update the user interface.

output_examples.input: My chat message listing is slow for large threads.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend paged message listing with a maximum page size and incremental loading in the application.

best_practices: Use short-lived user access tokens and implement secure refresh logic outside the client examples.
Use pagination for large threads to reduce latency and memory use.
Send read receipts only after the user has actually viewed the message.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode real user access tokens in source code or prompts.
Do not load every message in a large thread without pagination.
Do not expose system messages as user messages without filtering by message type.

faq.question: Does this skill create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It documents Java SDK usage after an Azure Communication Services resource and user token already exist.

faq.question: Can it help with real-time chat features?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers threads, messages, participants, read receipts, and typing notifications.

faq.question: Does it include authentication guidance?
faq.answer: It shows token credential usage, but it does not implement secure token issuance or refresh services.

faq.question: Is this skill specific to Java?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use the Azure Communication Services Chat Java SDK.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code or Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does it provide production-ready code?
faq.answer: No. It provides focused examples that need application-specific validation, security handling, and testing.
